title: The ILO's annual conference in Geneva: what happens in June
author: Editorial Desk
summary: Two weeks every June, 187 member States, one agenda on the world of work.
body:
Each June, ministers, employers and trade union leaders gather in Geneva for the **International Labour Conference (ILC)**. This is the supreme body of the ILO.

## How it works

- Each member State sends a delegation of four: two from the Government, one from employers and one from workers.
- Delegates sit in committees that discuss technical items and in the plenary that adopts conventions, recommendations and the budget.
- A convention is adopted by a **two-thirds majority** of votes cast. Member States are then expected to consider ratifying it.

## The workers' group

Workers' delegates from each country form the **Workers' Group**, which coordinates positions. BMS, as one of the most representative central trade unions of India, has taken part in the Conference, and its leaders have spoken in committees and in plenary on subjects such as social protection, informality and decent work.

## The 2025 agenda

The 113th session in June 2025 held the first discussion on **decent work in the platform economy**, with a view to a convention and recommendation. A second discussion is due in 2026. That is the topic of the next post.
